name: Abbé de Marolles
summary: Three-player 66-card Tarot game from 1637 with declarations, Tarot bonuses and ultimo scoring.
rules_text: Three players use a 66-card pack: 22 triomphes (trumps I-XXI plus Fool), and in each suit K Q C J plus 7-4 in Swords/Batons and A-7 in Cups/Coins. Deal is 21 cards to each player after revealing bottom card. Non-dealers discard 1, dealer discards 4; discards count for owner, trumps and Tarots (K, Fool, I, XXI) may not be discarded. Before play players may declare for payment from both opponents: Tarots 1 marque for first 4 plus 1 per extra; Kings+Fool: 3K=1, 4K=3, Fool=1 extra; 10+ trumps (Fool counts) =1/2/3; Imperial: 4 courts of one suit or 4 Queens/Cavaliers/Jacks =1 each; Brizigole: run of 4-6 top or bottom trumps =1/2/3; all three triumph Tarots =3 or 2 holders ask qui-a-le-sien for 1. Trick play anticlockwise must follow suit, else must trump, highest trump or suit led wins. Fool is excused, cannot win or be lost, shown and kept. Every time a Tarot wins a trick holder gains 1 from each, if captured pays 1. Ace of Coins pays 1 when played. Last trick: winning with K or Pagat (I) gains 6, losing with it pays 6. Finally count card points in threes: Tarots 5, Q 4, C 3, J 2, plus 1 per 3 empties; highest total wins difference, lowest pays.
rating_reason: Specific historic trick-taking tarot game, turn-based
